summary: Timeboxed privileged access request for cross-customer session-linkage investigation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer-reported anomaly: a key customer reports that a small percentage of inference sessions appear to include tokens referencing a second customer's identifiable resource name. Customer Support flagged potential cross-customer linkage in prod session logs and asked for an internal privileged trace to validate.

Impact:
- Possible PII/cross-tenant linkage affecting two enterprise customers in us-west production cluster.
- Reported by Customer A (enterprise) as impacting compliance posture — needs quick validation.
- Low volume (estimated 0.02% of sessions) but high severity from compliance perspective.

Request / Justification:
- Timeboxed privileged access to a targeted set of prod traces / KV-cache slices to confirm whether session linkage is a platform bug (routing/cache leak) or a customer-provided prompt artifact.
- Scope limited to: session IDs listed in the 'Data requested' section below and any immediate parent/child request metadata needed for correlation. No full account dumps.

Data requested (explicit):
- Inference request/response headers and truncated payloads for session IDs: sess-2026-02-27-87a2, sess-2026-02-28-bf11, sess-2026-03-01-0c9d (three initial seed sessions).
- KV cache deltas for the serving runtime shard handling these sessions (time window: +/− 2 minutes).
- Routing decision logs and model variant fallbacks for the same timeframe.

Access controls proposed:
- Dual-approval: SRE lead (Devon Ortega) + Security reviewer (Priya Sethi) must sign off before any decrypt/rehydration actions.
- Access performed in a bastion session with screen recording and command logging enabled.
- Scoped role: temporary privileged-read only; no ability to export bulk payloads.
- Timebox: 8 hours of access starting after approvals are granted; access will be revoked automatically by our access gateway.

Audit & Minimization:
- Every action will be logged and checkpointed into an evidence bundle attachable to the ticket.
- Any tokens or PII will be redacted in-place; raw payloads remain encrypted and will not leave the secure bastion.

Acceptance criteria:
- Able to conclusively determine whether the observed linkage is due to platform-level KV cache routing or customer-supplied content overlap.
- Produce a short investigation note and next-step recommendation: bug fix, customer remediation guidance, or false-positive closure.

Customer contact for context (CS):
- Customer A account lead: Jordan Klein (jordan@customer-a.example) — provided sample session IDs and a redacted transcript excerpt.
- CS rep: Fiona Liu
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Re-run the sampling query used by CS to extract sessions (note: privileged query; do not run without approval).
2) For one sample session in the list, fetch serving-runtime routing trace via /internal/debug/route?id=<session-id> (access only via bastion).
3) Inspect KV cache keys for collisions around the target sequence numbers.
4) Cross-reference tokenization outputs for overlapping substrings that could cause apparent linkage.

investigation_notes:
Initial triage (Devon): Pulled routing sample for sess-2026-02-28-bf11 from the routing-logs index; no obvious cross-tenant header present. KV cache delta returned two keys with similar prefixes—one map entry included an escaped customer resource string. Hypothesis: collision caused by non-namespace-prefixed temporary keys from an older runtime optimization. Checked node assignment and found shard rebalancing at 2026-02-28 01:42 UTC which coincides with the suspect timeframe.

Action items before access:
- Get dual-approval + written customer consent.
- Prepare a minimized extraction script that redacts payloads and only returns token index ranges and hashed identifiers.

Preliminary risk assessment: medium — plausible platform-origin leakage via cache key namespace bug. If confirmed, mitigation might be to roll a key-prefixing patch and invalidate affected cache buckets.
resolution_notes:
(Pending) - Awaiting Security + SRE approvals and customer written consent. Planned next steps once approvals obtained: 1) Execute minimized extraction via bastion with screen recording. 2) Collect and store evidence bundle in secure evidence store path (secure://evidence/INT-100100/). 3) If platform leakage confirmed, schedule emergency patch for key-prefixing with a canary rollout in us-west, and notify affected customers with remediation steps.

Post-action follow-ups expected:
- If no platform issue found, create a CS-facing summary and recommended customer-side sanitization guidance.
- If platform issue found, raise INT/P0 incident ticket for rollout and customer notification.
